subject: Physics
statement: A body is thrown vertically upwards. Which one of the following graphs correctly represent the velocity vs time?

options.label: A
options.text: Linear decreasing graph passing through zero into negative velocity

solutionText: When a body is thrown vertically upward, acceleration is constant and directed downward (a = -g). The velocity-time equation is v = u - gt, which is a straight line with negative slope (-g) and positive y-intercept (u).

subject: Physics
statement: Object A is project from ground with speed 100 m/s and B is dropped from height 50 m then the time when they will collide is;
solutionText:
Object A projected upwards: s1 = 100t - 0.5 g t^2 = 100t - 5t^2
Object B dropped from height 50 m: s2 = 0.5 g t^2 = 5t^2
They collide when s1 + s2 = 50 m
(100t - 5t^2) + 5t^2 = 50 => 100t = 50 => t = 0.5 sec = 1/2 sec.
Final Answer: Option C (1/2 sec).

subject: Physics
statement: A body is projected vertically upward from the surface of the earth, its velocity-time graph is:

options.label: B
options.text: V-t graph 2 (straight line with negative slope)

solutionText: During vertical projection under gravity, acceleration is constantly -g. Velocity changes linearly according to v = u - gt. The graph is a continuous straight line with negative slope -g.

subject: Physics
topic: Kinematics - Free Fall and Released Packets
statement: A helicopter rises from rest on the ground vertically upwards with a constant acceleration g. A food packet is dropped from the helicopter when it is at a height h. The time taken by the packet to reach the ground is close to [ g is the acceleration due to gravity]
solutionText:
When the helicopter reaches height h with acceleration g from rest:
v^2 = 0 + 2gh => v = \sqrt{2gh} (directed upward).
For the dropped packet:
Taking ground as origin:
0 = h + vt - 0.5 g t^2
0 = h + \sqrt{2gh} t - 0.5 g t^2
0.5 g t^2 - \sqrt{2gh} t - h = 0
t = [\sqrt{2gh} + \sqrt{2gh + 4(0.5g)(h)}] / g = [\sqrt{2gh} + \sqrt{4gh}] / g = (\sqrt{2} + 2) \sqrt{h/g} ≈ (1.414 + 2) \sqrt{h/g} = 3.414 \sqrt{h/g} ≈ 3.4 \sqrt{h/g}.

subject: Physics
statement: The effective acceleration of a body when thrown upwards with acceleration a is
solutionText:
To find the effective acceleration of the body, we analyze the directions of the accelerations acting on it:
Upward Acceleration (a): The body is actively thrown or propelled upwards with an acceleration of a.
Downward Acceleration (g): The acceleration due to gravity always acts vertically downwards towards the Earth.
Since these two accelerations act in exactly opposite directions along the vertical line of motion, the net or effective upward acceleration is: Effective Acceleration = a − g.

subject: Physics
statement: A car travel half the distance with constant velocity of 40 kmph and the remaining half with a constant velocity of 80 kmph. The average velocity of the car in kmph is:
solutionText:
Avg velocity = Total displacement / Total time
= x / [(x/2)/40 + (x/2)/80] = 2 * 40 * 80 / (40 + 80) = 6400 / 120 = 160/3 = 53.3 km/hr.

subject: Physics
statement: If displacement of a particle is zero, the distance covered :

options.label: B
options.text: May or may not be zero

correctAnswer: May or may not be zero
solutionText: If the particle remains at rest at the starting position, both distance and displacement are zero. If the particle moves along a closed path and returns to its starting point, displacement is zero but distance is non-zero. Hence, distance covered may or may not be zero.

subject: Physics
statement: A particle moves along a semicircle of radius 10 m in 5 seconds. The average velocity of the particle is:
solutionText:
Average Velocity = Displacement / Time.
For a particle moving along a semicircle of radius r = 10 m:
Displacement = diameter = 2r = 2 * 10 = 20 m.
Time = 5 s.
Average Velocity = 20 / 5 = 4 m/s.
Correct option: D (4 ms−1).

subject: Physics
statement: A body starts from rest with uniform acceleration. What is the ratio of the distance travelled by the body during the 4th and 3rd second?
solutionText:
For a body starting from rest (u = 0) with uniform acceleration a, distance travelled in the nth second is:
s_n = u + (a/2)(2n - 1) = (a/2)(2n - 1)
Distance during 4th second: s_4 = (a/2)(2*4 - 1) = 7a/2
Distance during 3rd second: s_3 = (a/2)(2*3 - 1) = 5a/2
Ratio s_4 / s_3 = (7a/2) / (5a/2) = 7/5.
Correct answer: A (7/5).

subject: Physics
statement: Two balls are projected from an inclined plane from point Q & P respectively as shown. Select the incorrect statement:- (During the time both remain in air)

options.label: A
options.text: Path of w.r.t. is straight line

solutionText: Path of projectile A w.r.t projectile B is a straight line since relative acceleration between two freely falling bodies under gravity is zero (a_rel = g - g = 0). Since relative acceleration is zero, relative velocity is constant and the relative path is a straight line, not parabolic. Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.

subject: Physics
statement:
Statement-1: Two stones are simultaneously projected from level ground from same point with same speeds but different angles with horizontal. Both stones move in same vertical plane. Then the two stones may collide in mid air.

Statement-2 : For two stones projected simultaneously from same point with same speed at different angles with horizontal, their trajectories may intersect at some point.

options.label: A
options.text: Statement-1 is true, statement- 2 is true and statement- 2 is correct explanation for statement-1.

options.label: B
options.text: Statement-1 is true, statement- 2 is true and statement- 2 is NOT the correct explanation for statement-1.

options.label: C
options.text: Statement-1 is true, statement- 2 is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Statement-1 is false, statement- 2 is true.

solutionText: Since both stones are projected simultaneously with the same speed from the same point at different angles, their horizontal and vertical velocity components differ. For them to collide, both their x and y coordinates must be identical at the same instant t. Since x1 = (u cos θ1)t and x2 = (u cos θ2)t, x1 = x2 requires θ1 = θ2, meaning identical trajectories. If θ1 ≠ θ2, x1 ≠ x2 for all t > 0, so they can never be at the same point at the same time. Hence, Statement-1 is false. Their geometric paths (trajectories) do intersect at a point, so Statement-2 is true. Correct answer: Option 4.

subject: Physics
statement: A projectile is projected with initial velocity (6i^ + 8j^) m/s. If g = 10 ms−2, then horizontal range is :
solutionText:
Given u_x = 6 m/s, u_y = 8 m/s, g = 10 m/s^2.
Horizontal range R = 2 * u_x * u_y / g = 2 * 6 * 8 / 10 = 96 / 10 = 9.6 m.
Correct Option: 2 (9.6 metre).

subject: Physics
statement: With what minimum acceleration can a fireman slide down a rope whose breaking strength is two thirds of his weight?
solutionText:
Using free body diagram:
mg - T = ma
Given T = (2/3)mg
mg - (2/3)mg = ma => (1/3)mg = ma => a = g/3.
Correct option: D (g/3).

statement: A weight W rests on a rough horizontal plane. If the angle of friction is θ, the least force that can move the body along the plane will be
solutionText: To move the body along a rough horizontal plane with angle of friction θ (where μ = tan θ), the limiting static friction force is f_s = μ W = W tan θ. Hence Option B.

statement: The mass of a lift is 500 kg. When it ascends with an acceleration of 2 m/s2, the tension in the cable will be g=10 m/s2
solutionText:
The lift accelerates upward at 2 m/s^2, so cable tension is:
T = m(g + a) = 500(10 + 2) = 500 * 12 = 6000 N. Correct Option: A.

subject: Physics
topic: Surface Tension & Soap Bubble Surface Energy
statement: The radius of a soap bubble is r. The surface tension of soap solution is S . Keeping temperature constant, the radius of the soap bubble is doubled. The energy necessary for this will be
solutionText: Soap bubble has 2 free surfaces: A1 = 2 * (4πr^2) = 8πr^2. Doubled radius r' = 2r => A2 = 2 * (4π(2r)^2) = 32πr^2. ΔA = 32πr^2 - 8πr^2 = 24πr^2. Work = S * ΔA = 24πr^2 S.

statement: When a system is taken from state a to state b along the path acb, it is found that a quantity of heat Q = 200 J is absorbed by the system and a work W = 80 J is done by it. Along the path adb, Q = 144 J. In above question, if U_d = 88 J, heat absorbed for the path db is if U_a = 40 J
solutionText: From path acb: ΔU = Q - W = 200 - 80 = 120 J. Along adb: Q = 144 J => W_adb = 24 J. Using loop relation and U_d = 88 J, U_a = 40 J gives Q_db = 72 J.

statement: One mole of a monoatomic ideal gas occupies two chambers of a cylinder partitioned by means of a movable piston. The walls of the cylinder as well as the piston are thermal insulators. Initially equal amounts of gas fill both the chambers at (P₀, V₀, T₀). A coil is burnt in the left chamber which absorbs heat and expands, pushing the piston to the right. The gas on the right chamber is compressed until to pressure becomes 32P₀. The final volume of left chamber is :-
solutionText: Right chamber undergoes adiabatic compression: P0 V0^(5/3) = (32 P0) V_R^(5/3) => V_R = V0/8. Total volume is 2V0, so V_left = 2V0 - V0/8 = 15/8 V0.

statement: Which of the following is least volatile?
solution_text:
Solution
Easy
Due to strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding among H2O molecules, water possesses anomalously high boiling point and significantly lower vapour pressure compared to group 16 hydrides (H2S, H2Se, H2Te) which only exhibit weaker van der Waals / dipole-dipole interactions. Hence, H2O is the least volatile.
subject: Chemistry

statement: In which of the following compound there is more than one kind of hybridization (sp, sp2, sp3) for carbon?
solution_text: CH₂=CH−CH=CH₂ contains only sp²-hybridised carbon atoms. H−C≡C−H contains only sp-hybridised carbon atoms. CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ contains only sp³-hybridised carbon atoms. In CH₃−CH=CH−CH₃, the two terminal carbon atoms of the CH₃ groups are sp³-hybridised, while the two carbon atoms involved in the double bond are sp²-hybridised. Thus, this compound contains more than one type of hybridisation, namely sp² and sp³. Answer: D
subject: Chemistry

statement: During change of O2 to O2− ion, the electron adds to which of the following orbital.
solution_text:
Solution
Medium
The ground-state electronic configuration of O₂ (16 electrons) according to Molecular Orbital Theory is:
σ1s² σ*1s² σ2s² σ*2s² σ2pz² (π2px² = π2py²) (π*2px¹ = π*2py¹).
The lowest unoccupied / partially filled molecular orbital (LUMO/SOMO) is the antibonding π* orbital (π*2px or π*2py). When an additional electron is added to form the superoxide ion O₂⁻ (17 electrons), it enters into the π* antibonding molecular orbital.
subject: Chemistry

statement: Predict the correct order among the following:

options.text: Lone pair − bond pair > bond pair − bond pair > lone pair – lone pair
Lone pair − lone pair > lone pair − bond pair > bond pair – bond pair
Lone pair – lone pair > bond pair − bond pair > lone pair – bond pair
Bond pair − bond pair > lone pair − bond pair > lone pair – lone pair

solution_text:
Solution
Easy
Show Video Sol.
According to VSEPR theory, repulsive interaction of electron pairs decreases in the order:
Lone pair – lone pair (lp–lp) > Lone pair – bond pair (lp–bp) > Bond pair – bond pair (bp–bp).
Lone pairs are localized on the central atom under the influence of only one nucleus, occupying more spatial volume and exerting greater repulsion than bonded pairs shared between two nuclei.
subject: Chemistry

statement: Which of the following has fractional bond order :
solution_text:
Solution
Easy
1. O₂²⁺ (14 electrons, isoelectronic with N₂): Bond Order = (10 - 4)/2 = 3 (integer)
2. O₂²⁻ (18 electrons): Bond Order = (10 - 8)/2 = 1 (integer)
3. F₂²⁻ (20 electrons): Bond Order = (10 - 10)/2 = 0
4. H₂⁻ (3 electrons): Electronic configuration σ1s² σ*1s¹. Bond Order = (Nb - Na)/2 = (2 - 1)/2 = 0.5 (fractional).
subject: Chemistry

statement: Which of the following species does not contain unpaired electrons?
solution_text:
Solution
Easy
- B₂ (10 e⁻): π2px¹ = π2py¹ (2 unpaired electrons, paramagnetic)
- N₂⁺ (13 e⁻): σ2pz¹ (1 unpaired electron, paramagnetic)
- O₂ (16 e⁻): π*2px¹ = π*2py¹ (2 unpaired electrons, paramagnetic)
- O₂²⁻ (peroxide ion, 18 e⁻): all molecular orbitals including π*2px² and π*2py² are fully paired (0 unpaired electrons, diamagnetic).
subject: Chemistry

statement: Which of the following molecules has more than one lone pair?
solution_text:
Solution
Easy
Show Video Sol.
In XeF₂ (xenon difluoride), Xenon has 8 valence electrons, shares 2 with fluorine atoms (2 bond pairs), leaving 6 non-bonding electrons which constitute 3 lone pairs on the central Xe atom (sp³d hybridization, linear geometry). In SO₂ there is 1 lone pair on S; in SiF₄ and CH₄ there are 0 lone pairs on the central atom.
subject: Chemistry

statement: The bond between two identical non-metal atoms has a pair of electrons:

options.text: transferred fully from one atom to another

solution_text:
Solution
Easy
When two identical non-metal atoms form a chemical bond (such as H₂, Cl₂, O₂), they have identical electronegativities (ΔEN = 0). As a result, the shared electron pair is attracted equally by both nuclei, forming a pure non-polar covalent bond with equal electron density sharing.
subject: Chemistry

statement: Maximum no. of hydrogen bonds formed by an H2O molecule in ice is
solution_text:
Solution
Easy
Show Video Sol.
In ice, each H₂O molecule can form a maximum of four hydrogen bonds: two via its own hydrogen atoms (donors) and two via the lone pairs on its oxygen (acceptors). This extensive tetrahedral H‐bonding network is responsible for ice’s lower density compared to liquid water.
subject: Chemistry

statement: The vapour pressure of o-nitrophenol at any given temperature is predicted to be

options.text: higher or lower depending upon the size of the vessel

solution_text:
Solution
Easy
Show Video Sol.
o‐Nitrophenol predominantly exhibits intramolecular hydrogen bonding, reducing intermolecular forces and making its molecules easier to vaporize. By contrast, p‐nitrophenol forms intermolecular H‐bonds, causing stronger associations in the liquid and lower vapor pressure. Hence o‐nitrophenol has higher vapor pressure at a given temperature.
subject: Chemistry

comprehension: Answer Qs. 1-1 based on Comprehension: 20 g of N2 at 300K is compressed reversibly and adiabatically from 20 dm3 to 10 dm3.
statement: Calculate the final temperature
solution_text:
Solution
Easy
V1 = 20 L, V2 = 10 L
n = 20/28 = 5/7 mol
T1 = 300 K; q = 0 (adiabatic)
N2 is a diatomic gas: γ = 7/5
For reversible adiabatic process:
T1 * V1^(γ-1) = T2 * V2^(γ-1)
T1 / T2 = (V2 / V1)^(γ-1)
300 / T2 = (10 / 20)^(7/5 - 1) = (1/2)^(2/5)
T2 = 300 * (2)^(2/5) = 395.85 K ≈ 396 K.
subject: Chemistry

statement: In an isothermal expansion of an ideal gas
solution_text:
Solution
Easy
For an ideal gas, internal energy is solely a function of temperature: U = f(T). In an isothermal process, the temperature remains constant (ΔT = 0), which implies that the internal energy of the ideal gas remains constant: ΔU = 0.
subject: Chemistry

statement: For a system in equilibrium ΔG = 0 under conditions of constant
solution_text:
Solution
Easy
According to classical thermodynamics, the criterion for spontaneity and thermodynamic equilibrium at constant temperature and constant pressure is defined by Gibbs free energy: (dG)_{T, P} ≤ 0. At equilibrium, (dG)_{T, P} = 0.
subject: Chemistry

statement: Internal pressure of a perfect gas (ideal gas) is
solution_text:
Solution
Easy
Internal pressure π_T is defined as (∂U/∂V)_T. For an ideal gas, there are no intermolecular forces of attraction or repulsion between the gas molecules, meaning internal energy is independent of volume at constant temperature. Therefore, π_T = (∂U/∂V)_T = 0.
subject: Chemistry

statement: The value of Δn for the combustion reaction of one mole of benzene in gaseous state when both the reactants and products are at 298 K is
solution_text:
Solution
Easy
Combustion reaction with all species in the gaseous state:
C6H6(g) + 15/2 O2(g) -> 6 CO2(g) + 3 H2O(g)
Moles of gaseous products = 6 + 3 = 9
Moles of gaseous reactants = 1 + 15/2 = 8.5
Δng = n_p(g) - n_r(g) = 9 - 8.5 = +0.5 = 1/2.
subject: Chemistry

statement: For which change ΔH ≠ ΔE
solution_text:
Solution
Easy
Show Video Sol.
Relationship: ΔH = ΔE + Δng RT.
For ΔH = ΔE, Δng must be zero.
In option (1): Δng = 2 - (1 + 1) = 0 => ΔH = ΔE.
In option (3): Δng = 1 - 1 = 0 => ΔH = ΔE.
In option (4): Δng = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2 ≠ 0 => ΔH ≠ ΔE.
subject: Chemistry

statement:
Find the work done when 18ml of water is getting vapourised at 373 K is open vessel

(Assume the ideal behaviour of water vapour.)
solution_text:
Solution
Easy
Show Video Sol.
Given:
Volume of water = 18 mL, Density = 1 g/mL => Mass = 18 g
Moles of water: n = 18 / 18 = 1 mol
At 373 K, ideal gas behavior:
PV = nRT
Work done during vaporization in an open vessel against atmospheric pressure:
w = -P ΔV ≈ -P V_gas = -nRT
w = -(1 mol) * (0.0821 L atm mol^-1 K^-1) * (373 K) ≈ -30.62 L atm ≈ -30 L atm.
subject: Chemistry

statement: Out of the following, the correct statement is:

options.text: ΔE = q + w for every thermodynamic system at rest in the absence of external field

solution_text:
Solution
Easy
Show Video Sol.
Internal energy E is a state function. In a cyclic process, the system undergoes a series of transformations and returns to its initial state (State 1 -> State 2 -> ... -> State 1). Therefore, the overall change in internal energy is identically zero: ΔE = 0.
subject: Chemistry

statement:
If 1/2 X2O(s) → X(s) + 1/4 O2(g) : ΔH = 90 kJ.

Then heat change during reaction of metal X with one mole of O2 to form oxide to maximum extent is
solution_text:
Solution
Easy
Given reaction:
1/2 X2O(s) -> X(s) + 1/4 O2(g) : ΔH = +90 kJ
Reversing the reaction:
X(s) + 1/4 O2(g) -> 1/2 X2O(s) : ΔH = -90 kJ
For reaction of metal X with 1 mole of O2 to form oxide, multiply the entire equation by 4:
4 X(s) + O2(g) -> 2 X2O(s)
ΔH_reaction = 4 * (-90 kJ) = -360 kJ.
subject: Chemistry

statement: Adiabatic expansion of ideal gas into vacuum correspond to
solution_text:
Solution
Medium
Show Video Sol.
In free adiabatic expansion of an ideal gas into vacuum:
1. Expansion into vacuum means P_ext = 0, so work done w = -P_ext * ΔV = 0.
2. Adiabatic conditions mean heat transfer q = 0.
3. By the First Law of Thermodynamics: ΔE = q + w = 0 + 0 = 0.
4. Since ΔE = 0 for an ideal gas, temperature does not change (ΔT = 0). Consequently, ΔH = ΔE + Δ(PV) = ΔE + nRΔT = 0.
Therefore, all of these statements (w = 0, ΔE = 0, ΔH = 0) are correct.
subject: Chemistry
Chemistry
statement:
On decomposition of $\text{NH}_4\text{HS}$, the following equilibrium is established

$$\text{NH}_4\text{HS}(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{NH}_3(g) + \text{H}_2\text{S}(g)$$

If the total pressure is $P\text{ atm}$, then the equilibrium constant $K_P$ is equal to
solution_text:
On decomposition of solid ammonium hydrogen sulphide:
$$\text{NH}_4\text{HS}(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{NH}_3(g) + \text{H}_2\text{S}(g)$$
Since solid $\text{NH}_4\text{HS}$ does not contribute to gas pressure and produces equimolar amounts of $\text{NH}_3(g)$ and $\text{H}_2\text{S}(g)$:
$$p_{\text{NH}_3} = p_{\text{H}_2\text{S}} = \frac{P_{\text{total}}}{2} = \frac{P}{2}\text{ atm}$$
Now, applying the equilibrium constant expression in terms of partial pressures:
$$K_P = p_{\text{NH}_3} \times p_{\text{H}_2\text{S}} = \left(\frac{P}{2}\right) \times \left(\frac{P}{2}\right) = \frac{P^2}{4}\text{ atm}^2$$
Therefore, option (3) is correct.

subject: Chemistry
statement: Number of $\text{H}^+$ ions present in $10\text{ mL}$ of a solution of $\text{pH} = 3$ is:
solution_text:
Given:
$\text{pH} = 3 \implies [\text{H}^+] = 10^{-\text{pH}} = 10^{-3}\text{ mol/L}$
Volume of solution $V = 10\text{ mL} = 10 \times 10^{-3}\text{ L} = 10^{-2}\text{ L}$
Moles of $\text{H}^+$ ions $n = [\text{H}^+] \times V = 10^{-3}\text{ mol/L} \times 10^{-2}\text{ L} = 10^{-5}\text{ mol}$
Number of $\text{H}^+$ ions = $n \times N_A = 10^{-5} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 6.02 \times 10^{18}\text{ ions}$
Therefore, the correct answer is option (2).

subject: Chemistry
statement: At $80^\circ\text{C}$, distilled water has $[\text{H}_3\text{O}^+]$ concentration equal to $1 \times 10^{-6}\text{ mole/litre}$. The value of $K_w$ at this temperature will be
solution_text:
For pure distilled water at any temperature:
$$[\text{H}_3\text{O}^+] = [\text{OH}^-]$$
Given $[\text{H}_3\text{O}^+] = 1 \times 10^{-6}\text{ mol/L}$, so $[\text{OH}^-] = 1 \times 10^{-6}\text{ mol/L}$.
The ionic product of water $K_w$ is defined as:
$$K_w = [\text{H}_3\text{O}^+][\text{OH}^-] = (1 \times 10^{-6}) \times (1 \times 10^{-6}) = 1 \times 10^{-12}\text{ mol}^2\text{L}^{-2}$$
Therefore, the correct answer is option (3).

subject: Chemistry
statement:
$K_{a1}$, $K_{a2}$ and $K_{a3}$ are the respective ionisation constants for the following reactions:

1) $\text{H}_2\text{S} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+ + \text{HS}^-$
2) $\text{HS}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+ + \text{S}^{2-}$
3) $\text{H}_2\text{S} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{H}^+ + \text{S}^{2-}$

The correct relationship between $K_{a1}$, $K_{a2}$, $K_{a3}$ is:
solution_text:
Adding reaction (1) and reaction (2):
$$\text{H}_2\text{S} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+ + \text{HS}^- \quad (K_{a1})$$
$$\text{HS}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+ + \text{S}^{2-} \quad (K_{a2})$$
----------------------------------------------------
$$\text{H}_2\text{S} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{H}^+ + \text{S}^{2-} \quad (K_{a3})$$
When chemical equations are added, their equilibrium constants multiply:
$$K_{a3} = K_{a1} \times K_{a2}$$
Therefore, option (1) is correct.

subject: Chemistry
statement: The conjugate base of hydrazoic acid is :
solution_text:
Hydrazoic acid has the chemical formula $\text{HN}_3$.
According to Bronsted-Lowry acid-base theory, the conjugate base of an acid is formed when the acid donates a proton ($\text{H}^+$):
$$\text{HN}_3 \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+ + \text{N}_3^-$$
Here $\text{N}_3^-$ is the azide ion, which is the conjugate base of hydrazoic acid.
Therefore, option (2) is correct.

subject: Chemistry
statement: Which of the following is not a Lewis acid?
solution_text:
A Lewis acid is an electron pair acceptor.
- $\text{BF}_3$: Boron has an incomplete octet (6 valence electrons), so it readily accepts a pair of electrons (strong Lewis acid).
- $\text{FeCl}_3$: Fe has vacant d-orbitals and incomplete valence shell, accepting electron pairs.
- $\text{SiF}_4$: Silicon can expand its octet using vacant 3d orbitals to form $[\text{SiF}_6]^{2-}$, so it behaves as a Lewis acid.
- $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ (ethene): Ethene possesses an electron-rich $\pi$-electron cloud. It acts as an electron donor (Lewis base or nucleophile), not as an electron acceptor.
Therefore, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ is not a Lewis acid. Option (2) is correct.

subject: Chemistry
statement: $1.1\text{ mol}$ of $A$ mixed with $2.2\text{ mol}$ of $B$ and the mixture is kept in a $1\text{ L}$ flask and the equilibrium, $A + 2B \rightleftharpoons 2C + D$ is reached. If at equilibrium $0.2\text{ mol}$ of $C$ is formed then the value of $K_C$ will be
solution_text:
Given volume $V = 1\text{ L}$. Thus moles equal molar concentrations.
Reaction: $A + 2B \rightleftharpoons 2C + D$
Initial: $[A]_0 = 1.1\text{ M}$, $[B]_0 = 2.2\text{ M}$, $[C]_0 = 0$, $[D]_0 = 0$
At equilibrium, $[C] = 2x = 0.2\text{ M} \implies x = 0.1\text{ M}$.
Then:
$[D] = x = 0.1\text{ M}$
$[A] = 1.1 - x = 1.1 - 0.1 = 1.0\text{ M}$
$[B] = 2.2 - 2x = 2.2 - 2(0.1) = 2.0\text{ M}$
Now calculating $K_C$:
$$K_C = \frac{[C]^2 [D]}{[A] [B]^2} = \frac{(0.2)^2 \times (0.1)}{(1.0) \times (2.0)^2} = \frac{0.04 \times 0.1}{1.0 \times 4.0} = \frac{0.004}{4.0} = 0.001$$
Therefore, option (3) is correct.

subject: Chemistry
statement: Which of the following are Lewis bases?
solution_text:
A Lewis base is a chemical species that cannot only accept protons but can donate a pair of electrons.
- $\text{AlCl}_3$: Electron-deficient central aluminium atom (6 valence electrons) makes it a classic Lewis acid.
- $\text{Br}_2$: The halogen molecule possesses non-bonding lone pairs of electrons and can donate electron density to act as an electron-pair donor toward suitable acceptors; in this standard JEE classification, it acts as a Lewis base.
- $\text{H}^+$: Has a completely vacant orbital and no electrons, acting exclusively as a Lewis acid.
- Alcohols ($R-\text{O}-\text{H}$): The oxygen atom possesses two lone pairs of electrons and donates an electron pair, acting as a Lewis base.
Therefore, options (2) and (4) are correct.

subject: Chemistry
statement: At $25^\circ\text{C}$, the dissociation constant of a base $\text{BOH}$ is $1.0 \times 10^{-12}$. The concentration of hydroxyl ions in $0.01\text{M}$ aqueous solution of the base would be
solution_text:
For a weak monobasic base $\text{BOH}$:
$$\text{BOH} \rightleftharpoons \text{B}^+ + \text{OH}^-$$
With initial concentration $C = 0.01\text{ M} = 10^{-2}\text{ M}$ and $K_b = 1.0 \times 10^{-12}$.
Since $K_b$ is very small, degree of dissociation $\alpha \ll 1$:
$$[\text{OH}^-] = \sqrt{K_b \times C} = \sqrt{(1.0 \times 10^{-12}) \times (10^{-2})} = \sqrt{1.0 \times 10^{-14}} = 1.0 \times 10^{-7}\text{ mol L}^{-1}$$
Therefore, the concentration of hydroxyl ions is $1.0 \times 10^{-7}\text{ mol L}^{-1}$. Option (2) is correct.

subject: Chemistry
statement:
In a reaction

$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_4(g) + \text{H}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{C}_2\text{H}_6(g)$$

the equilibrium constant can be expressed in units of
solution_text:
The unit of equilibrium constant $K_C$ is given by:
$$\text{Unit of } K_C = (\text{mol L}^{-1})^{\Delta n_g}$$
For the reaction:
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_4(g) + \text{H}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{C}_2\text{H}_6(g)$$
$$\Delta n_g = n_p - n_r = 1 - (1 + 1) = 1 - 2 = -1$$
Substituting $\Delta n_g = -1$:
$$\text{Unit of } K_C = (\text{mol L}^{-1})^{-1} = \text{mol}^{-1}\text{ L} = \text{L mol}^{-1}$$
Therefore, option (2) is correct.

subject: Chemistry
statement: Oxidation number of Cl in CaOCl2 is:
solution_text:
In bleaching powder, CaOCl₂ exists as Ca²⁺(OCl)⁻(Cl)⁻.
In the hypochlorite ion (OCl)⁻: O(−2) + Cl(x) = −1 ⇒ x = +1.
In chloride ion Cl⁻: Cl = −1.
Therefore, the two chlorine atoms have oxidation states of −1 and +1.

subject: Chemistry
statement: The oxidation state of a metal in a compound is represented according to the notation which is known as
solution_text: The German chemist Alfred Stock introduced the system of indicating the oxidation state of a metal in a compound by Roman numerals in parentheses after the symbol of the metal, known as Stock notation (e.g., Fe(II)SO₄, Fe(III)Cl₃).

subject: Chemistry
statement:
3KClO3 + 3H2SO4 ⟶ 3KHSO4 + HClO4 + 2ClO2 + H2O

Equivalent weight of KClO3 is

options.option_text: M + M/2 (or M/1 + M/2 = 3M/2 per mol reaction, giving Eq wt = M + M/2)

solution_text:
In 3KClO₃, chlorine (+5) undergoes disproportionation:
1 mol KClO₃ oxidises to HClO₄ (+7) -> change = 2 (n-factor = 2), Eq wt = M/2
2 mol KClO₃ reduce to 2ClO₂ (+4) -> change per mol = 1 (n-factor = 1), Eq wt = M/1
Total equivalent weight of disproportionating salt = Eq(ox) + Eq(red) = M + M/2.

subject: Chemistry
statement: 0.52 g of a dibasic acid required 100 mL of 0.2 N NaOH for complete neutralization. The equivalent weight of acid is
solution_text:
Given:
Mass of dibasic acid = 0.52 g
Volume of NaOH = 100 mL = 0.1 L
Normality of NaOH = 0.2 N
Equivalents of base = N × V = 0.2 × 0.1 = 0.02 eq.
At complete neutralization:
Equivalents of acid = Equivalents of base = 0.02 eq.
Equivalent weight = Mass / Equivalents = 0.52 / 0.02 = 26 g/eq.
Hence, Option 1 (26) is correct.

subject: Chemistry
statement: How many electrons should X2H4 liberate so that in the new compound X shows oxidation number of −1/2 (E.N. X > H)
solution_text:
In X₂H₄, with E.N. of X > H:
Each H is +1.
2(x) + 4(+1) = 0 ⇒ 2x = −4 ⇒ x = −2 (initial oxidation state of each X).
For the molecule X₂H₄, total initial charge on the two X atoms = 2 × (−2) = −4.
In the new compound, oxidation state of X is −1/2.
Total charge on the two X atoms in the product = 2 × (−1/2) = −1.
Change in total charge = (−1) − (−4) = +3.
Therefore, 3 electrons must be liberated.

subject: Chemistry
statement: Oxidation state of nitrogen is correctly given for:
solution_text:
A. In Mg₃N₂: Mg is +2. 3(+2) + 2x = 0 ⇒ 2x = −6 ⇒ x = −3. Correct.
B. In NH₂OH: x + 3(+1) + (−2) = 0 ⇒ x = −1 (not +1). Incorrect.
C. In (N₂H₅)₂SO₄: N₂H₅⁺ has 2x + 5(+1) = +1 ⇒ 2x = −4 ⇒ x = −2 (not +2). Incorrect.
D. In [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂: NH₃ is a neutral ligand where N has oxidation state −3, not 0. Incorrect.
Therefore, Option 1 is correct.

subject: Chemistry
statement: The oxidation state of Fe in Fe3O4 is
solution_text:
Fe₃O₄ is a mixed oxide (FeO·Fe₂O₃).
Let average oxidation state of Fe = x.
3x + 4(−2) = 0
3x = +8
x = +8/3.
Hence, the average oxidation state of Fe in Fe₃O₄ is +8/3.

subject: Chemistry
statement:
The equivalent weight of KIO3 in the reaction, 2Cr(OH)3 + 4OH⁻ + KIO3 → 2CrO4²⁻ + 5H2O + KI

is
solution_text:
(i) In this redox reaction, KIO₃ acts as an oxidising agent.
(ii) In KIO₃, oxidation state of I is: +1 + x + 3(−2) = 0 ⇒ x = +5.
In product KI, oxidation state of I is −1.
Change in oxidation number of iodine per formula unit = (+5) − (−1) = 6.
Therefore, n-factor = 6.
Equivalent weight = Molecular weight / 6.

subject: Chemistry
statement: When K2Cr2O7 is converted to K2CrO4, the change in the oxidation state of chromium is
solution_text:
In K₂Cr₂O₇:
2(+1) + 2x + 7(−2) = 0 ⇒ 2x = 12 ⇒ x = +6.
In K₂CrO₄:
2(+1) + x + 4(−2) = 0 ⇒ x = +6.
Both compounds have chromium in the +6 oxidation state.
Therefore, the change in the oxidation state is 6 − 6 = 0 (this is an acid-base equilibrium reaction, not a redox reaction).

subject: Chemistry
statement: When chlorine is passed into hot conc caustic soda solution the oxidation number of chlorine was increased in one of the products from:
solution_text:
When chlorine is passed into hot concentrated NaOH solution, disproportionation occurs:
3Cl₂ + 6NaOH → 5NaCl + NaClO₃ + 3H₂O
Oxidation number of chlorine in Cl₂ = 0.
In NaClO₃: (+1) + x + 3(−2) = 0 ⇒ x = +5.
Thus, chlorine undergoes oxidation from 0 to +5.
Simultaneously, chlorine is reduced from 0 to −1 in NaCl.
Hence, the oxidation number was increased from 0 to +5.

subject: Chemistry
statement: Which of the following is not an electrophile?
solution_text: Electrophiles are electron-deficient species (Lewis acids or positively charged ions/electron-deficient molecules like CH₃⁺, AlCl₃ with an incomplete octet, and SiF₄ with vacant d-orbitals). Hydroxide ion (OH⁻) has unshared lone pairs and negative charge, acting as an electron-rich nucleophile, not an electrophile.

subject: Chemistry
statement:
Select the correct common name of the compound from:
CH3–CH(Cl)–CH2–CH3
solution_text: The compound is CH₃–CH(Cl)–CH₂–CH₃. The chloride substituent is attached to a secondary carbon (2° carbon) of a four-carbon butyl chain, giving the trivial/common name 'sec-butyl chloride'. Note: 2-chlorobutane is the IUPAC name, but the question specifically asks for the common name.

subject: Chemistry
statement: Which of the following represent incorrect numbering schemes according to IUPAC rules?
solution_text:
Incorrect numbering: B and D.
According to IUPAC lowest locant rule for unsaturated chains, double and triple bonds must receive the lowest locant set possible. Renumbering from the opposite terminus in B and D yields lower locants for multiple bonds, showing that B and D violate IUPAC numbering rules.

subject: Chemistry
statement: In which structure carbon does not act as an electrophile?
solution_text:
In CH₃–CH₂–Cl, the carbon attached to electronegative chlorine carries a partial positive charge (δ+) and acts as an electrophile.
In CH₃–CO–CH₃, the carbonyl carbon has δ+ due to C=O polarisation and acts as an electrophilic center.
In CH₃–CN, the cyano carbon has δ+ due to C≡N polarisation and acts as an electrophile.
In CH₃–MgBr (organometallic reagent), carbon is more electronegative than magnesium (C: 2.5 vs Mg: 1.2), giving carbon a partial negative charge (δ−, carbanionic character); therefore it acts as a nucleophile, not an electrophile.

subject: Chemistry
statement: A sample of 0.5 g of an organic compound was treated according to Kjeldahl's method. The ammonia evolved was absorbed in 50 mL of 0.5 M H2SO4. The remaining acid after neutralisation by ammonia consumed 80 mL of 0.5 M NaOH. The percentage of nitrogen in the organic compound is
solution_text:
Normality of H₂SO₄ = 2 × M = 2 × 0.5 = 1 N.
Total milli-equivalents of H₂SO₄ taken = 50 mL × 1 N = 50 meq.
Normality of NaOH = 1 × 0.5 = 0.5 N.
Milli-equivalents of unreacted H₂SO₄ = 80 mL × 0.5 N = 40 meq.
Milli-equivalents of H₂SO₄ consumed by ammonia = 50 − 40 = 10 meq.
Percentage of Nitrogen = (1.4 × meq of acid consumed) / (mass of compound in g)
% N = (1.4 × 10) / 0.5 = 14 / 0.5 = 28%.
Hence, Option 2 (28%) is correct.

subject: Chemistry
statement: Give the IUPAC name of the compound (cyclohexene ring with a double bond at C1 and methyl substituents at C1, C3, and C3):
solution_text: The double bond in the cycloalkene takes priority and receives positions 1 and 2. Numbering from the double bonded carbon containing the methyl group gives C1 with one methyl group and C3 with two methyl groups. This produces the lowest locant set (1, 3, 3). The IUPAC name is 1,3,3-trimethylcyclohex-1-ene.

subject: Chemistry
statement:
The IUPAC name of the following compound is:
H3C–CH2–CH(CH2CH3)–CH2–CH(CH3)–CH2CH3
solution_text:
The longest continuous carbon chain contains 7 carbon atoms (heptane).
Substituents are located at positions 3 and 5 from either direction: an ethyl group and a methyl group.
When numbering from either end gives identical locants (3, 5), the alphabetical priority rule decides: 'ethyl' comes before 'methyl' alphabetically, so the ethyl group gets the lower locant 3 and the methyl group gets 5.
Hence, the correct IUPAC name is 3-ethyl-5-methylheptane.

subject: Chemistry
statement: Which of the following compounds contains only 2∘ carbon atoms?
solution_text:
A secondary (2°) carbon atom is directly bonded to two other carbon atoms.
In cyclohexane (C₆H₁₂), each carbon is a –CH₂– ring member connected to two neighboring carbon atoms; hence all six carbons are secondary (2°).
Pentane contains two 1° (terminal) and three 2° carbons.
2-methylpentane contains 1°, 2°, and 3° carbons.
Methylcyclopentane contains a 3° ring junction carbon and a 1° methyl carbon.
Therefore, Option 4 (Cyclohexane) is correct.

subject: Chemistry
statement:
The IUPAC name for the given compound is:
CH3–CH=CH–CH2–CH(Cl)–CH3
solution_text:
The principal functional group/unsaturation is the C=C double bond, which takes precedence over halogen substituents.
Numbering must start from the end nearer the double bond:
C1–C2=C3–C4–C5(Cl)–C6
Double bond is at position 2 (hex-2-ene) and chlorine substituent is at position 5.
Therefore, the correct IUPAC name is 5-chlorohex-2-ene.

subject: Chemistry
statement:
In the following compounds the decreasing order of B.P. is:
(I) CH3−CH2−CH2−CH2−CH2−CH3 (n-hexane)
(II) CH3−CH(CH3)−CH2−CH2−CH3 (2-methylpentane)
(III) CH3−C(CH3)2−CH2−CH3 (2,2-dimethylbutane)
solution_text:
For isomeric alkanes having the same molecular formula (C₆H₁₄):
As branching increases, the molecule becomes more compact and spherical, reducing the surface area of contact between adjacent molecules.
This decreases van der Waals (London dispersion) forces, leading to a lower boiling point.
Therefore:
Straight-chain n-hexane (I) has the largest surface area and highest boiling point.
Monobranched 2-methylpentane (II) has intermediate boiling point.
Dibranched 2,2-dimethylbutane (III) has the most spherical shape and lowest boiling point.
Decreasing order of boiling point: (I) > (II) > (III).
